newsitem.title: USA: Two top Columbia/HCA executives resign.
newsitem.headline: Two top Columbia/HCA executives resign.

text.p: Richard Scott resigned Friday as chairman of Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., the giant for-profit hospital chain being investigated for fraud by federal regulators.
Resigning along with Scott, who founded Columbia, was President and Chief Operating Officer David Vandewater, the company said.
Half a dozen federal agencies are probing the operations of Columbia/HCA, examining Medicare-billing practices, home health-care operations, recruitment of physicians, and other matters.

Last week, a spokesman for the Justice Department said 35 search warrants had been served in seven states -- Florida, Texas, Tennessee, North Carolina, Utah, Oklahoma and Georgia -- for hospitals owned or formerly owned by Columbia and two companies doing business with the chain.
Thomas Frist Jr., vice chairman of the Columbia/HCA board, was named to succeed Scott as chairman and chief executive officer, the company said.
Frist's family started Hospital Corporation of America, the parent of HCA. He owns 14.6 million shares, or about 2.2 percent of Columbia, now valued at $529 million.
According to company filings in March, Scott owns 1.4 percent of Columbia shares, valued at about $340 million at Thursday's closing stock price of $36.25.
According to a report in Friday's New York Times, Frist, a career hospital executive, was said to be displeased by Scott's aggresive operating style.

One analyst was quoted in the paper as saying Scott "expanded (Columbia) in such an antagonistic style that the Government, the payers, the physicians and the not-for-profit hospitals are completely focused on him as the Darth Vader of the industry."

In announcing the resignations, Columbia/HCA said, "Both executives (Scott and Vandewater) emphasised that throughout their tenure they have acted honourably and in the best interests of the company."

Frist said in a statement, "Our board and management will be focusing on providing full cooperation with all governmental agencies. We will also ensure that all Columbia facilities and employees are in full compliance with the law."
Columbia stock was up 81.25 cents at $37 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
